summary: "chat-early" is the owner's conversation with Claude Code from 2026-07-21 to 2026-08-15, preserved as `notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md` (455 turns, 446 genuine researcher turns; 9 flagged as harness-injected compaction summaries) plus 12 full-transcript chunks (`chunks/chunk_01..12.md`, ~6MB total, manifest at `chunks/MANIFEST.md`). The raw JSONL is gone, so these files are primary source. The period covers the project from the moment an uploaded 121-file zip was committed into `xuvictor04/LLM-Test` through the creation of the `notes/DOC_PLAN.md` documentation mandate that produced the notes corpus itself. The arc runs: naming/handoff hygiene → build and test "Verification" (reconstruction) → discover it dies on the base-rate wall → scale data and lose a day of H100 compute to a missing checkpoint → build a JEPA-style world model → performance work and GPT-2 as a rough benchmark → repeated reframes away from domain/clustering metrics toward language output and continual learning → expert-population work (router discovery, weight-predicting router, chaining) on a new branch `rm-predict` → tokenizer/minting work → a "disentangle the levers" refactor program → per-expert learning rates and evolutionary culling. Roughly 18% of the "user turns" (81 of 455) are `stop-hook-git-check.sh` echoes, not researcher input. The owner ran every GPU experiment himself on rented cloud boxes and pasted results back; the assistant's container was CPU-only and ephemeral.

facts.claim: NORTH STAR in the owner's own words (given via AskUserQuestion, 2026-07-21): "The genie wish is an LLM capable of learning, complex reasoning, much smaller than conventional models, and with an ever expanding and updatable knowledge base. Realistically there will be compromises. When this occurs, expansion and growability are not to be lost. It also need to be capable of language, as a personal benchmark. WIth this concept, a goal is the ability for multimodality, where we can plug in and add more avenues, and a dashboard to stream and see the thinking and processes occuring"

Training from scratch (not on a pretrained base) was chosen for "Novelty / full ownership"; compute is "rented, so as long as necessary."; success priorities are "covo [conversation], sentence generation, architecture, shipping in order of most to least important"
Goal A restated as a hard priority: "The final goal will always be proper language, working on top of that."
Goal A restated again: "Remember, the ultimate goal is textual, not arbitrary metrics." and "Output quality will always trump other metrics. They, however are useful for my design sake."

Goal B stated in the owner's words: "The end all is the resulting output, and capacity for continual learning without exorbitant forgetting, and maintaining old capacities, without significant degradation. The project should reflect this."

Both goals reasserted against tokenizer optimization: "the final goal is for language, not optimizing specifically the tokenizer, vmax, or different ways to freeze the structure... Remember that a target has been and still is the continual learning."

Anti-metric-optimization constraint: "I don't want to optimize for our arbitrary metrics. Their use is only as proxies, so we can quickly tell how close we are from getting to proper language, and continual learning capabilities... If a metric isn't working, but the system itself is improving, that does not mean the system is at wrong, but the metrics and how we are using them."

Multimodality design: "Sense" means a modality, not polysemy — "Sense was supposed to be a separate thing, where currently it is built as an LLM, but multimodal in and output can be created. Ie I attach a mic to the system, giving it a new sense"

Modalities enter at the tokenizer layer: "Senses should be integrated via the lowest tokenizer layer, and “discovered” when unknown or unusual inputs are recieved, before reconciliation, and understanding"

Core architectural intent — work must be subdivided, not done by one component: "I don't want the full task to be done alone. Ideally it is subcontracted in a sense, and spread out, via the router base." and "On the interchangeability, ideally, subspecialties will emerge, for specific tasks, breaking things down"
Experts may terminate in tool calls: "some “experts” can end in a tool call/pre established scripts (but capable of being created by the system itself if done often enough) like a token"

Routers-as-embedders is an owner idea from day one: "Maybe routers can act like embedders, taking an input (and source), modification, then embedding to determine which expert is most similar, or from learned recognition, allowing it to transfer to prior unknown parts"

Surprise and reverse embedders were intended as learning-signal machinery: "Surprise was supposed to be a mechanic to facilitate the ongoing learning" / "Reverse embedders, a part of it, for a certain level of thought, verification, or training"

Rejected design: strict per-domain memory quota. "I don't like a strict per domain quota. The system sounds like it will break something. Likely, a better way is if memory burden is near, the domain can be expanded in terms of experts, possibly retrain the experts, or a sign as domain splitting is needed"

Memory design directive: per-expert memory, quota counted in entries not bytes, 16-128 entries, LRU by last use. "it should be keyed such that each expert has their own, and they have a max quota. Not in terms of bytes or bits. It should be in number of entries... possibly 16 to 128 max entries. (Ranked on when last utilized)"
Expert population scale expectation: "I don't understand why experts is capped at 64, my expectation is much higher. Thousands or even millions. Selection at a scale of tens is pointless."
Breadth cap directive: "Cap the number of domains a single expert can be part of. It should be percentage based." plus "We can cull domains when they are empty."

Evolutionary growth directive: "Growth should not just be the fittest, since a more niche may be more relevant. Newborn should also have some randomness / mutation injected" and "We can add on to the randomness mechanism by allowing (completely random) new experts to take random connected sections of other experts."
Router discovery declared the critical gap: "The router issue is very big. We need to fix it, inability to discover a new expert is almost catastrophic to the idea. How can we do it?"

The `rm-predict` mechanism in the owner's words: "Can we use this system for expert creation and discovery? Where routers output its desired expert (by weights), and we will route to closest, but if there is a wildly different, than the predicted to be, for the new to be created. This way routers can be trained to discover and created. Accordingly, backprop for routers will work with the new weights of the experts"

Router input/exit directive: "I want the router fabric input to include the source's weights. Since that's the only way to know where it's from. The router should be the one who determines when to complete, not go directly from expert to head."
Chaining is the default path: "Make sure whenever I run, it is including chaining, unless specified otherwise." and "Use the most updated, use the chaining society, it should be the default."
The owner's own definition of chain_vote: "my idea for chain_vote was the society system, but allowed to loop over and over, (in chains)"
Tokenizer minting is load-bearing for goal B: "Token minting is critical for my idea of continual learning."

Minted tokens must inherit parameters, not start cold: "We want minted tokens to start with parameters. My original goal was to make the transition, between new mint and its composite, much easier. I want these tokens to be trained on even with the loss, but we need to do it differently." — reversing his own earlier suggestion of integer-value ids

Final LR/culling spec of the period: "Lets use Smith's Cyclical LR, but implemented in a per expert scale then, with each expert counting down their age. Lets adjust things to only be when the specific expert is selected, so age is dependent on the expert's use. Lets make the safe period dependent on this instead, and modify the culling percentv from the either 8% or 4% that it currently is to 2% or 1%. I want to keep LR independent for each expert."

Culling is non-negotiable but must be balanced: "Balance loss can be implemented on a smaller scale. I still want culling since it is semicritical to our evolutionary mechanism. Balance will help ensure that each expert has a chance."

Bottom-ranked experts should get more LR or mutation, but only outside their safe phase: "SInce we have the custom learning rates per expert, lets have a mechanism, where if the expert is near bottom, it has an increased LR or mutation chance" ... "For 5, on the bottom ranked experts, this is assuming they are outside of their safe phase."

If they contain error, ideally, they will eventually be replaced by their own \"new successors\", with long enough runs. Importantly, having LR Epochs as a per expert effect rather than system encompassing is more conductive to the evolutionary learning"

levers.name: VERIFY / VERIFY_SWEEP / RECON_W
levers.effect: VERIFY selects the wrongness signal ("selfcon" default vs "recon"); VERIFY_SWEEP deletes unverified entries from the store; RECON_W turns on joint training of the Reconstructor (0.0 = off).
couples_with: the surprise write gate (base rate of corrupt entries)
levers.evidence: notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md:2586 ("VERIFY=os.environ.get(\"VERIFY\",\"selfcon\")", RECON_W default 0.0); run output at :573-:574

levers.name: TOK_ONLINE / SEED_VOCAB / VMAX
levers.effect: Online mint-on-repetition tokenizer. SEED_VOCAB is only a seed; VMAX is the true cap. Owner ran capless (uncapped VMAX), 4k and 8k arms as an experimental spread.
couples_with: LOSS_MASK_DEAD (dead softmax rows scale with VMAX)
_total_steps / LR schedule (measured once at seed vocabulary)
levers.evidence: notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md:3353 ("SEED_VOCAB is a seed, VMAX is the true cap"); :11001; :10365-:10368

levers.name: TOK_MINT_UNTIL
levers.effect: Freezes minting at the given step. Does NOT stop re-segmentation: at TOK_MINT_UNTIL=1 a "frozen" run still fired 39 no-op re-tokenizations.

levers.name: TOK_ANCHOR / TOK_ANCHOR_TAU / TOK_ANCHOR_USES / TOK_COMPOSE
levers.effect: ByteComposer gives a minted token vector = composite(bytes) + zero-init residual, with a decaying penalty on the residual. TOK_ANCHOR_USES (owner-set to 400) releases the anchor by appearances rather than steps — but it is gated on TOK_COMPOSE, whose default is 0, so it is inert at default.
couples_with: RETOK_EVERY (owner asked resegmentation not to fire inside the anchor period)

levers.name: TOK_MINT_PMIN / TOK_MINT_GATE_K / TOK_MINT_NOVEL
levers.effect: Branching-entropy merge gating before minting (p(b|a) threshold, top-K pair pool). TOK_MINT_PMIN defaults to 0 and fails open; TOK_MINT_NOVEL defaults to 0.0, making the novelty branch inert.
levers.evidence: notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md:11002; chunk_08.md:5385 ("f9d676c ... gated on `if self.novel > 0` ... Banner: TOK_MINT_NOVEL=0. Inert.")

levers.name: SOCIETY / CHAIN_ROUTE / CHAIN_VOTE
levers.effect: Selects the forward path: society() one-hop blend at prediction level; CHAIN_ROUTE=transition (learned transition matrix); CHAIN_ROUTE=soc (society re-routed each hop, default). CHAIN_VOTE makes experts vote each hop with HALT mass choosing which hop's answer is used. CHAINED SOCIETY = SOCIETY=0 + CHAIN_ROUTE=soc + CHAIN_VOTE=1.
couples_with: MEM_PER_EXPERT, competence EMAs, spawn_from, sustained-error culling — all were SOCIETY-gated and therefore off under chaining
DIV_W and IND_W (not runnable on a composed walk)

levers.name: FAB_N0 / FAB_NMAX / FAB_GROW / FAB_COOLDOWN
levers.effect: Expert population: initial size, hard cap (raised to 4096), growth on/off, and a blackout window after a detected shift during which PlateauGrowth cannot grow. Owner ran 2048-start vs growth-from-small as the "growth vs size" series.
couples_with: PlateauGrowth ramp latch (`n >= ramp_to * cap` — starting at the soft cap disarms the ramp)

levers.name: EXP_DOM_FRAC / EXP_DOM_MIN / CHAIN_BAN
levers.effect: The percentage-based breadth cap the owner asked for (dom_ban returns a hard -inf routing mask). It reads fab.dom_of, which was populated one sample per step, so the cap could only ever ban the ~30 experts that happened to be sampled — effectively inert from the day it was added until commit 99e5da0 fixed the table.

levers.name: MEM_CAP / MEM_QUOTA / MEM_OWNERS / MEM_PER_EXPERT / WRITE_TARGET
levers.effect: Editable memory: capacity, per-expert entry quota (owner: 16-128, LRU by last use), owner bucket = expert id folded modulo MEM_OWNERS, and the surprise-quantile write target that right-sizes the store.
couples_with: SOCIETY (MEM_PER_EXPERT was SOCIETY-gated and silently off under chaining)

levers.name: KEY_SRC + rekey (REKEY_CHUNK, amortized rekey)
levers.effect: Memory keys come from the model's own representation (KEY_SRC=model) and must be periodically re-keyed as the model drifts; the amortized rekey spreads that cost across steps. In the A100 bench, rekey(amortized) was 48-49% of step time at d=768.

levers.name: SIG_MODE / SIG_SPACE / SIG_WIN / ENC_WARMUP / ENC_WARMUP_MIN / ENC_EVERY_IDLE
levers.effect: SigEncoder domain-fingerprint encoder (InfoNCE over byte or token windows). ENC_WARMUP_MIN is the adaptive-warmup floor; contrastive_step is shift-gated (every step near a boundary, every ENC_EVERY_IDLE=12 steps when stable) so its profile share is data-mix dependent.
couples_with: ENC_WARMUP (setting ENC_WARMUP_MIN == ENC_WARMUP makes the plateau test unreachable)
the data mix (encoder share is not transferable between corpora)
levers.evidence: notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md:7419; :3771-:3776 ("the encoder share is DATA-DEPENDENT, so do not carry the ~85% figure over")

levers.name: NEW_DIST / SHIFT_DIST / MAX_DOMAINS / SEG_MIN / SEG_MAX / WIN
levers.effect: Domain assembly thresholds and segment geometry. The thresholds are absolute constants while the encoder's distance scale inflates as it trains — the run's own diagnostic named this an "ASSEMBLER/threshold problem (raise NEW_DIST, or normalize distances per-domain)". SEGMENT/WINDOW below ~3 windows per splice makes clustering scores describe transitions, not domains.
levers.evidence: notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md:4728-:4730; :6382 ("!! CONFIG WARNING: SEGMENT/WINDOW = 1250B / 384B = 3.3 windows per splice segment")

levers.name: ROUTE_GROUNDED / ROUTE_T / ROUTE_REGION_W
levers.effect: Grounded routing. ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 ROUTE_T=0.3 reproduces the "modularity" regime from the same code as the "redundancy" regime — a config difference, not a code difference. ROUTE_REGION_W weights the grounded-region cosine against the weight-prediction term in entry_logits.
couples_with: ground_update (EMA centroid buffer, no_grad — not backprop)
the weight-prediction term the owner asked to be the main consideration
levers.evidence: notes/_evidence/chat/user_turns.md:57 (regime reproduction via two env vars); :2560; :9672; :10352

levers.name: CKPT_EVERY / SAVE_CKPT / RESUME / BEST_TRACK
levers.effect: Mid-run checkpointing every N steps plus SIGUSR1 checkpoint-on-demand, added after a full day of H100 compute was lost to an end-only save. BEST_TRACK writes a `.best` snapshot on held-out improvement but never restores it.
couples_with: repeat/seeds harness modes (SAVE_CKPT=0 also disables holdout_bpb, changing what the run measures)

levers.name: EPOCHS / LR_EPOCHS / LR_RESTARTS / LR_DECAY
levers.effect: Cosine LR wavelength in epochs (default 8, clamped min(8, EPOCHS)), number of whole cycles fitted to the run, and a decaying envelope added later. _lr_at reads _total_steps, measured once at the seed vocabulary; _proj_steps re-projects live but is used only in the ETA print, not the schedule.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-21 — The project entered this chat as an upload, not as a repo. A 121/122-file zip was committed into the empty repo `xuvictor04/LLM-Test`; because the repo was empty, the import branch `claude/hub-addition-1ueehb` became the repository's default branch. The owner was migrating from a prior chat he could no longer compress.
carry_forward.why: Explains why there is no `main`, why the default branch has a Claude-generated name, and why the earliest project history exists only as prose the owner pasted forward.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-21 — `handoff/` was created at repo root on the owner's spec: "Each idea should have separate folders or files. The target is to assume that the next message will blank, relying on it", with filenames as the index. STATE.md remained the single source of truth rather than being duplicated.
carry_forward.why: This is the ancestor of the notes/ corpus and the reason context is organized one-idea-per-file. The stated design assumption — the next reader starts blank — still governs.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-21 — Naming was locked: B -> Verification, Fabric -> Router + Compositor (Fabric 'retired'), Expert -> Sub-skill -> Tool-expert, Domain kept, Sense = modality (NOT polysemy; polysemy became 'Meaning'). The Fabric retirement did not survive contact with the code.
carry_forward.why: Anyone reading old docs will hit 'Router + Compositor' and 'B' and needs the mapping; and needs to know that 'fabric' is still the live term.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-21/22 — Verification-by-reconstruction was built, validated standalone (AUC 0.980 / precision@1% 100% vs self-consistency B at 0.907 / 36.9%), and then failed in the product loop at 0.3% precision. Two wrong root causes were proposed (joint-training-on-churn, then undertraining) before the correct one: the BASE-RATE WALL — at <1% corruption injection, any signal's false-positive rate sinks precision. VERIFY reverted to `selfcon` by default.
carry_forward.why: This is the canonical example of a mechanism that measured beautifully in isolation and did nothing in situ. Any future store-wide wrong-detection proposal must answer the base-rate question first.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-22 — The owner flagged that short runs may make all results misleading: "I am concerned, however, that some results may be misleading since the runs are so short." Data was scaled 6M -> 30M -> 40M byte streams in response, and the corpus moved from NLTK to HuggingFace ("Why not use a set of data from hugging face?").
carry_forward.why: Establishes early that run-length is a standing confound on every number in this project, by the owner's own reckoning.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-23 — A ~day-long H100 run finished with no checkpoint. pyrasite failed; a gdb attach to force a save hit SIGSEGV because the process spends nearly all its time in CUDA with the GIL released. The day was lost. `CKPT_EVERY=N` mid-run saves and a SIGUSR1 checkpoint-on-demand handler were added afterwards; the owner said "I am surprised that we stopped checkpointing. The estimates given are always wrong and longer than expected."
carry_forward.why: The single most expensive incident of the period, and the origin of the checkpointing machinery. Also the origin of the owner's recurring 'You keep on turning off checkpoints' complaint (2026-08-14).

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-23/24 — The world model was requested and built as JEPA/VICReg-style latent forward dynamics: predict the *representation* of the future, not tokens or pixels. The owner's constraint was that it be a general world model, not a model of its own situation, and that it be 'more like the rest of the system, in its separation'. Physics was later downgraded from requirement to illustration.
carry_forward.why: Fixes the design intent of WORLD_MODEL/WORLD_FEEDBACK/WORLD_GROW: modality-agnostic latent prediction, structured like the expert population.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-24 — Performance work was authorized ("let's make the system more efficient") and immediately produced the 'no compromise' correction: removing sections and running only 'tested and approved' paths to gain speed is not acceptable. GPT-2 was adopted as the rough benchmark (~124M params, ~8B tokens, ~1.0-1.2 b/B; the system was ~29M params at D_MODEL_B=768 and ~2.0 b/B). An mmap disk-streaming loader was built to break the RAM ceiling.
carry_forward.why: The 'no compromise' rule is a standing constraint that recurs for the rest of the period; the GPT-2 numbers are the reference frame for every bits/byte figure.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-24/25 — Expert and memory design turns: per-expert memory with an entry-count quota (16-128, LRU by last use); chaining to be allowed by default; sparse top-k routing; capacity expansion horizontally or vertically; rapid initial growth preferred over delayed growth. The owner also asked to 'clarify on what is an expert, since I imagined it as series of layered neural networks'.
carry_forward.why: These are the design commitments the expert population is supposed to satisfy, and the 'what is an expert' question was never fully closed — low-rank A/B adapters are what got built.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-25 — GH200 acquired. probe_signature.py built. The domain-assembly failure was root-caused to a scale-free-vs-absolute-threshold mismatch: NEW_DIST/SHIFT_DIST are constants while the encoder's distance scale inflates as it trains. The run's own diagnostic distinguished 'ASSEMBLER/threshold problem' from 'ENCODER problem'.
carry_forward.why: This is a unit-mismatch of exactly the class the DID IT FIRE audit hunts, and it is the reason domain counts swing from 1 to 547 across otherwise similar runs.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-25 — KEY REFRAME: the four seeded domains (eng/py/num/c) were always the arbitrary part. "My view was these domains are naturally overlapping, and instead make it self assembling." Optimizing clustering purity against those labels is optimizing against a fiction.
carry_forward.why: Any note that reports purity/V-measure against the seeded labels as a success criterion is measuring the wrong thing by the owner's explicit statement.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-27/29 — Metric reframe #2: "I don't want to optimize for our arbitrary metrics. Their use is only as proxies... If a metric isn't working, but the system itself is improving, that does not mean the system is at wrong, but the metrics and how we are using them." probe_stability then found domain identity is not reproducible across seeds: "NO MORE THAN CHANCE. The two runs did not find the same structure."
carry_forward.why: Establishes both the epistemic rule and the concrete finding that kills domain identity as a target.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-29/31 — Harness era begins: rerun.sh (mix / eng / ablate / smoke arms, 2026-07-29) then longrun.sh (pilot regime, 2026-07-31). Defaults were changed so subsystems are ON by default after the owner found things silently off in prior tests ("Change defaults to have things on. Since things were off in prior tests, do we need a rerun?", asked four times).
carry_forward.why: Explains why the repo has two run harnesses and why 'is it actually on?' became a first-class question in every banner.

carry_forward.item: 2026-07-31 — KEY REFRAME #3, the clearest statement of the two goals: "domains are not a major concern for me... The end all is the resulting output, and capacity for continual learning without exorbitant forgetting, and maintaining old capacities, without significant degradation. The project should reflect this... My bigger concerns is within the domains, and the experts."
carry_forward.why: This is the sentence that defines the project's two definitive goals in the owner's own words, and it explicitly demotes everything else.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-02/03 — First pilots run. The 64-expert cap was rejected ("Thousands or even millions. Selection at a scale of tens is pointless"). Percentage-based breadth cap requested. Growth must not be fitness-only ('a more niche may be more relevant'); newborns need randomness/mutation and may take random connected sections of other experts.
carry_forward.why: Defines the evolutionary contract for the expert population: diversity by construction, not just selection pressure.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-03/04 — Router discovery declared the critical failure: "The router issue is very big. We need to fix it, inability to discover a new expert is almost catastrophic to the idea." The answer became expert weight-embedders (eemb/edec) plus spawn_from: the router outputs a desired expert as weights, routes to the nearest, and if nothing is near, decodes the query into a new expert.
carry_forward.why: This is the mechanism the whole `rm-predict` branch exists for; it is the owner's own design, not a suggestion.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-04 — Branch change: "Since this is an interesting new mechanism, I'd like to have it be pushed as a separately named branch. Call it 'R M Predict'" then "I want you to be working on this branch from now on". All subsequent work is on `rm-predict`, not `claude/hub-addition-1ueehb`.
carry_forward.why: Anything read from the default branch after 2026-08-04 is stale; the live line of development is rm-predict.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-04/05 — Chaining landed and became the default path (SOCIETY=0 + CHAIN_ROUTE=soc + CHAIN_VOTE=1, 'chained society'). The owner's definition: 'the society system, but allowed to loop over and over, (in chains)'. HALT was found computed-and-discarded on the society path and had to be wired in.
carry_forward.why: The default forward path changed here; every earlier measurement was on a different path, and four subsystems were SOCIETY-gated and silently off under the new one.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-05 — The banner-lie / diverging-curve incident. A 48k-step chaining pilot had been getting worse for 91% of its length (3.56 @ 5903 -> 4.68 @ 47231) while the report said 'still FALLING = more passes/steps will help', and the banner claimed per-expert memory was ON when it had been off from step 0. The society pilot had the same shape. Owner: "Fix all banner lies... Make them automatic and based off what's run. Also have the exact pull branch be announced in each log."
carry_forward.why: The origin of the project's DID IT FIRE discipline: a mechanism reported as on, a verdict computed with the wrong sign, and a run whose headline was the opposite of the truth — all in the same log.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-05/06 — Focus shifts to the tokenizer. The owner probed why best bits/byte lands at step ~6k when minting has not capped, tested a minimum-sized tokenizer, and set the design rule: minted tokens must start with parameters (ByteComposer: composite(bytes) + zero-init residual, with a decaying TOK_ANCHOR penalty) so "the transition, between new mint and its composite" is easy. He explicitly reversed his own suggestion of using raw integer values as token ids. "Token minting is critical for my idea of continual learning."
carry_forward.why: Fixes why the tokenizer is not a side concern: minting is the owner's mechanism for goal B, and the parameter-inheritance rule is a hard design constraint on it.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-11 — The levers program. "I want you to normalize and disentangle the code, since there are so many interrelated things, some unnecessary. This way we have clearer levers... Ensure that nothing is functionally different." Produced: equiv.sh (behavioural-equivalence tool with a determinism self-test, 2026-08-10), a _SPEC knob registry (274 -> 279 knobs, `_env` raises SystemExit on default mismatch), and levers.py enforcing 100% coverage (2026-08-11). The first attempt was rejected and reverted; the determinism self-test then reported the machine is NOT deterministic.
carry_forward.why: This is why the codebase has a knob registry at all, and why the equivalence claims from that period are weaker than they look — the comparison tool's own precondition failed.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-11 — Token quality control built: branching-entropy merge gating (merge a,b when a reliably predicts b) defaulted ON, plus a probationary mechanism (TOK_PROBATION, retire() that pops from seq2id but leaves id2bytes). Anchor release moved from steps to appearances (TOK_ANCHOR_USES=400). LR schedule reworked: no clamp, repeating cosine, wavelength 8 epochs but running the whole length of the run.
carry_forward.why: These are owner-specified mechanisms with owner-specified defaults; TOK_ANCHOR_USES in particular is inert at default because TOK_COMPOSE=0, which is a live DID-IT-FIRE finding.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-12 — Restatement against tokenizer tunnel-vision: "the final goal is for language, not optimizing specifically the tokenizer, vmax, or different ways to freeze the structure. I need to be able to carry and build off the results we get, and a stumbling block has been the levers I've wanted split, but not, and interfering with our runs. Our capless vmax was supposed to be an experimental test... Min tokenizer was for the opposite end. Remember that a target has been and still is the continual learning."
carry_forward.why: Names the purpose of the capless/min-tokenizer arms (bracketing an unknown, not selecting a winner) and re-anchors on the two goals.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-13/14 — Seed-spread investigation. Same-config runs at seeds 0/1/2 differed markedly in both numbers and text quality; the owner suspected cross-run state leak ("is there anything that is being kept, saved, and possibly used in the following runs? It likely is not the tokenizer") and then reframed it: "state leak would be bad in one sense, however, we can utilize this for our system, building off of it (intentionally), to get more efficient. We still need to control for it when applicable, but it is a helpful lever."
carry_forward.why: An unresolved reproducibility problem that undermines every A/B in the period, plus an explicit owner instruction not to simply eliminate it.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-14/15 — Growth-vs-size series. FAB_N0=2048 with FAB_NMAX=4096 became a temporary baseline ("hopefully reproduce the 2048 results with the 4096. We can temporarily set it as the baseline"); growth burst reduced to 1 at 4% (cull is 8%); 4x larger English corpus; 18 epochs; a transformer arm (MODEL=transformer, LAYERS=4). Target: "safely below 2, ideally hit 1.5 this run."
carry_forward.why: The concrete configuration state at the end of the period, and the numeric bar the owner set.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-15 — Per-expert learning rates. "Lets use Smith's Cyclical LR, but implemented in a per expert scale then, with each expert counting down their age. Lets adjust things to only be when the specific expert is selected, so age is dependent on the expert's use. Lets make the safe period dependent on this instead, and modify the culling percent... to 2% or 1%." Implemented via update rescaling (Adam is invariant to constant gradient scaling). Bottom-ranked experts get increased LR or mutation chance, but only outside their safe phase. Balance loss added; culling explicitly retained as "semicritical to our evolutionary mechanism".
carry_forward.why: The last architectural commitment of the period, and it converts a global training schedule into a per-expert lifecycle keyed to use — a structural change to how continual learning is supposed to work.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-15 — Memory isolation failure found: "the fact that the memories from the python run has largely overwritten the english, it means that the domains have not been fully isolated. Better memory control is likely also needed." Owner's diagnosis: "overlap experts is ok and expected, but having all experts have been overlapped is an inherent issue. Likely separation or distinction, on router level between python and english is not sufficient. Use based recency is better I think."
carry_forward.why: This is a direct catastrophic-forgetting observation on goal B, made by the owner from the run output, and it is unresolved at the end of the period.

carry_forward.item: 2026-08-15 — Research and documentation agents launched. Five agents (LR schedules, MoE/expert routing, adaptive tokenization, continual learning + editable memory, and a documentation planner producing notes/DOC_PLAN.md). WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy for arxiv, OpenReview, ACL, SemanticScholar and HuggingFace, so almost nothing was read in full and nearly every claim is memory-tagged rather than fetched. Owner: "Since webfetch was blocked, provide me what to tell a non claude code session... (also it should alert me if something is blocked)", then supplied an external report himself.
carry_forward.why: Every literature claim written into notes/ during this period carries an evidence tag for a reason: the sources were mostly not readable. And DOC_PLAN.md is the direct parent of this documentation task.

carry_forward.item: Standing operating rules for anyone working this repo, verbatim from the owner: default to bash unless python is specified; assume a fresh box each run; git through a python console so it pastes from a phone; confirm before acting on performance changes; no compromises (do not remove or downgrade functionality for speed); work on rm-predict; treat every past comment as a rough statement, never as definitive.
carry_forward.why: These recur across every compaction boundary in the period and are the closest thing the project has to a contract.
